A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AutoURDF work and support reliable textual and visual comparison. v1 includes Appendices A–C; the supplied v2 ends after the references and omits those appendices despite retaining appendix references. This omission is observable in the supplied files.

before.justification: v1 reports original robot reconstruction experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, real-world scanning results, and additional household-object and sensitivity experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original synthetic and real-world robot experiments, including Tables 1–3 and qualitative reconstruction results, and adds a qualitative NPP comparison.

M1.justification: The core robot pipeline and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. However, v2 omits the household-object variant in Appendix C.3 that incorporates point normals into k-means clustering. This narrows the documented method variants; the missing architecture appendix does not establish a redesign of the retained network.

E1.justification: The eight-robot synthetic evaluation and real WX200 scan remain. Appendix C.3's evaluation on six household objects—laptop, trashcan, toilet, dishwasher, faucet, and storage cabinet—is absent from v2, removing a distinct application domain. The related-work change from Sapien to PartNet-Mobility does not establish replacement evaluation data.

E2.justification: Figure 7 adds NPP to the qualitative comparison on the same ten-frame robot sequences. The quantitative comparator set in Table 1 remains Reart and MultiBodySync; MBS is an abbreviation of the existing MultiBodySync baseline.

E3.justification: The omitted supplementary experiments remove protocols comparing rotation representations across ten sequences at angular steps of 4–10 degrees and testing eleven cluster counts per robot. The retained evaluation still uses ten-frame, 5,000-point sequences and the same one-versus-five-sequence comparison. No revision to those retained settings is established.

E4.justification: v2 omits the rotation-representation stability study in Appendix B.4/Figure 16 and the cluster-count sensitivity study in Appendix C.2/Figure 18. These remove substantial evidence about representation choice and hyperparameter robustness. The main Step/Anchor, position/orientation, and sequence-count analyses remain.

E5.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their Mean±Std reporting, and Figure 9 retains averaging across sequences and shaded variation bands. No changed seed, repeated-run, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is specified. Figure 16's error bars disappear together with the entire experiment, rather than through a revised reporting practice for retained results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 are numerically identical, including Table 1's AutoURDF mean CD of 9.63 and TED of 2.26. v2 adds qualitative NPP results but omits the rotation-loss results, cluster-count TED results, and household-object reconstructions in Figures 16, 18, and 19. The reported outcomes therefore become substantially narrower.

T1.justification: The core mathematical formulation, Equations 1–3, and revolute-joint/tree-structure assumptions remain unchanged. The omitted standard silhouette formulas explain an existing procedure. v2's Euler-rotation-theorem sentence adds conceptual explanation without a new formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim unsupervised construction of simulator-compatible URDFs from point clouds and improved registration and topology accuracy for complex robots. The contribution bullets are shortened, but the abstract, introduction, novelty claim, and conclusion retain the same scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting shared-network processing to input-order independence and revolute-motion parameterization to URDF compatibility. It loses supplementary interpretations concerning rotation stability, cluster-count robustness, and the faucet's segmentation difficulty despite accurate joint prediction. The three main limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: The omitted appendices remove the detailed network architecture, positional encoder, optimizer and learning rates, early stopping, topology pseudocode, and sequence-merging instructions. They also remove synthetic camera/noise specifications and the iPhone scanning and preprocessing workflow. These are substantial reproducibility losses, especially because v2 still directs readers to the absent appendices.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hayden et al.'s NPP reference and removes the supplementary references for Adam, Scaniverse, and Fourier features. Related work more specifically describes how Watch-It-Move and Reart reanimate models. The central positioning around unsupervised reconstruction and simulator-compatible descriptions remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 edits introduction and methodology prose, shortens contribution bullets, clarifies notation, renames Section 3.5 to URDF Generation, and replaces numbered discussion subsections with inline headings. It also updates affiliation text and adds acknowledgements. The main narrative order remains stable.

P2.justification: All supplementary Figures 12–20 and Algorithm 2 disappear, removing data-collection diagrams, architecture documentation, analyses, and reconstruction galleries. Main figures also receive revised rendering, labels, color scales, and typography; Figure 7 gains an NPP column. Figure 9 is restyled while retaining its plotted findings.

improvement.justification: Within the supplied PDFs, clearer exposition and the added qualitative NPP comparison are outweighed by the omission of Appendices A–C. v2 loses essential reproduction details and substantial evidence about robustness and household-object applicability while retaining unresolved appendix references. With the main quantitative results unchanged, these losses substantially weaken the paper's completeness and verifiability.
